title: [ORION-QG QG-27] Bulk-defect law and thermodynamic cost density for all-n TARE
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Direct parents: QG-23 #879 / PR #882 auxiliary-support compactness; QG-26 #884 / PR #885 guarded histogram geometry.
Related parent: QG-25 #881 (older generic tropical spectral programme; QG-27 is a stronger TARE-specific route on exact scaling rays).
Method donors: thermodynamic limits, surface/boundary corrections, finite-defect expansions, subextensive corrections, lower envelopes of finitely many affine functions.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE BULK–DEFECT / THERMODYNAMIC-LIMIT THEOREM — freeze before execution.**

QG-26 earns, for every valid fixed-matching histogram `N in N^4096`,

`C_DP(N) = min_{tau feasible} [B_{pi(tau)}(N) + K_tau]`,

with an optimum whose nontrivial auxiliary letters occupy at most six physical columns. There are 8 target-permutation baselines, collapsing in QG-26 to 4 exact vectors.

This implies the auxiliary optimization is a finite **defect correction** on top of an extensive spectator/bulk baseline.

## Q1 — universal all-n defect band

Define

`B_min(N) = min_pi B_pi(N)`.

For any QG-23-normalized accepted template with `k<=6` active columns:
- its structural frame/Tag term, including the frozen `-18` offset, is at least 2 because all six frames are nonzero and the shared Tag has support at least 1;
- each active column replaces one spectator two-branch F3 baseline in `[0,6]` with another two-branch F3 value in `[0,6]`, so its local correction lies in `[-6,+6]`.

Hence every accepted normalized template obeys

`K_tau >= 2 - 6*k >= -34`.

Therefore

`C_DP(N) >= B_min(N) - 34`.

For the upper bound, choose a target-permutation pi attaining `B_min(N)` and any physical target column type present in N. On that one coordinate use any of the exact 48 feasible one-qubit shared-label frame/Tag rows from QG-24/QG-26; use identity auxiliary letters everywhere else. The one-active structural term is exactly 2 and its F3 correction is at most +6. Therefore

`C_DP(N) <= B_min(N) + 8`.

Frozen candidate band:

`B_min(N)-34 <= C_DP(N) <= B_min(N)+8`

for every valid fixed-matching TARE histogram and every physical n.

The constants are deliberately crude universal bounds, not claimed sharp. A successor may tighten them only prospectively.

## Q2 — vanishing auxiliary density / thermodynamic limit

For any sequence of valid histograms `N^(m)` with total qubit count `n_m=sum_t N_t^(m) -> infinity` and empirical frequencies

`p_t = lim_m N_t^(m)/n_m`

existing componentwise, divide the Q1 band by `n_m` to obtain

`C_DP(N^(m))/n_m -> min_pi sum_t p_t b_pi(t)`.

Thus the exact asymptotic cost density is determined solely by the finite set of spectator baseline linear forms; all optimized frame/Tag structure is subextensive `O(1)`.

This may be called a **compiler thermodynamic-limit / bulk-density theorem**, not a physical thermodynamic phase transition.

## Q3 — exact scaling rays are eventually affine

Fix a valid integer histogram motif `h` such that every one of the six target components is nonzero somewhere in h. Let

`N(k)=k h`, `k>=1`.

By QG-26, every finite template tau is either:
- never feasible on the ray because it requires a column type t with `h_t=0`; or
- feasible for all `k >= K_tau = max_t ceil(m_tau(t)/h_t)` over its used types.

Whenever feasible,

`C_tau(kh)=k B_pi(h)+K_tau_const`.

The lower envelope of finitely many affine functions is eventually one affine function (or several identical/tied functions). Therefore there exist exact integers `K>=1`, slope `s` and intercept `q` such that

`C_DP(kh)=k*s+q` for every `k>=K`.

Moreover, because for every target permutation pi and every target type present in h there exists a one-active feasible shared-label template, the asymptotic slope is exactly

`s = min_pi B_pi(h)`.

So QG-27 strengthens the generic QG-25 expectation from eventual affine-periodicity to **eventual exact affinity with period 1** on pure repetition rays.

## Q4 — asymptotic count-space phase cells

For normalized frequency vectors p, define the four distinct QG-26 bulk forms `beta_r(p)` corresponding to the four distinct spectator baseline vectors.

The asymptotic density is

`e(p)=min_r beta_r(p)`.

Therefore the frequency simplex is partitioned by a finite normal-fan-like arrangement of exact linear tie hyperplanes into **bulk compiler phase cells**. These are asymptotic TARE cost-density mechanisms only.

QG-27 V1 may authorize existence of this four-form asymptotic phase geometry and exact tie equations. It must not claim finite-n global phase boundaries or physical phases.

## Q5 — complete local bound verification

Production and generic analyzers independently enumerate:
- all 4096 target column types;
- all 8 target permutations;
- all `4^7` local auxiliary-letter tuples;
- all 8 central tuples where relevant;
- all 48 one-active accepted auxiliary rows.

Required exact local controls:
1. spectator baseline range exactly `[0,6]`;
2. arbitrary active two-branch F3 range exactly `[0,6]`;
3. active F3 correction range exactly `[-6,+6]` over the complete local target/auxiliary domain;
4. structural term over every globally feasible support-capped auxiliary configuration is >=2 as a theorem from support/nonzero counts, with the one-active 48-row family attaining exactly 2;
5. for every target type and every target permutation, at least one one-active accepted row exists, so the +8 upper construction never depends on target chemistry/content.

No exhaustive global template universe is needed for the universal band.

## Q6 — frozen scaling-ray controls

Before execution freeze a small deterministic panel derived only from QG-26 baseline vectors:
- one unary valid motif if available; otherwise the lexicographically first valid motif of minimum support;
- one two-type motif where two distinct bulk forms tie;
- one motif strictly selecting each distinct baseline form when such a motif exists within a bounded search over histogram support <=2.

These controls are for exact slope/tie verification only. Do not fit K or q from them and promote globally.

## Independent generic ORION

Generic ORION must rebuild phase-free Pauli/F3 algebra and QG-26 baseline vectors independently, derive the local correction extrema and the `[-34,+8]` band independently, and verify the finite-lower-envelope argument on the frozen ray controls without importing production QG-27 code.

## Native ORION-Q

May authorize only:
- `BULK_DEFECT_UNIFORM_BOUND_ALL_N`;
- `ASYMPTOTIC_COST_DENSITY_EXACT`;
- `PURE_SCALING_RAY_EVENTUALLY_AFFINE`;
- `ASYMPTOTIC_COUNT_SPACE_PHASE_GEOMETRY`.

Mandatory false:
- `DEFECT_CONSTANTS_SHARP`;
- `FINITE_N_GLOBAL_PHASE_BOUNDARY`;
- `PHYSICAL_PHASE_TRANSITION`;
- `CHAIN_ALL_N`;
- `CLOSED_FORM_BDOUBLEPRIME_COMPLETENESS`;
- novelty/R6/physical-advantage authority.

## Intended strong terminal

`QG27_TARE_BULK_DEFECT_LAW_AND_EXACT_ASYMPTOTIC_COST_DENSITY_ALL_N_MACHINE_CHECKED`

Honest alternatives:
- `QG27_LOCAL_CORRECTION_BOUND_REFUTED`
- `QG27_ONE_ACTIVE_UPPER_CONSTRUCTION_GAP`
- `QG27_QG26_PARENT_BINDING_GAP`
- `QG27_GENERIC_NATIVE_DISAGREEMENT`
- `QG27_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Donor subtraction

Thermodynamic limits, finite-size/boundary corrections, lower envelopes of affine functions, normal fans and asymptotic density arguments are established mathematics and receive zero novelty credit. Candidate contribution is only the exact TARE-specific bounded-defect theorem, exact bulk cost-density law and period-1 eventual-affinity consequence. No physical thermodynamic claim is requested.
